metadata.title: Outpatient Intake 001
metadata.disclaimer: Fictional, synthetic, medically unreviewed prototype content; not authoritative treatment guidance.

sourceUseNotes.contribution: CANMAT Q.1.d supports a comprehensive, individualized assessment and a psychiatric and medical differential before MDD treatment. This informs the direction of these workup rules; it does not prescribe PsychSim's exact point values.

Developer opinion and game balance set the relative rewards, costs, and conditional penalty: substance history and medication reconciliation are useful, while missing mania history is penalized specifically when an antidepressant is started.

Developer opinion: workup relevance follows the submitted treatment. Starting an antidepressant activates mania history; starting any medication activates medication reconciliation and allergy/adverse-reaction history. A resolved prior reaction to the selected medication affects safety whether or not the player revealed that history. Exact point values and the generic reaction-severity mapping are provisional game balance.

CANMAT's initial-treatment sections support multiple first-line antidepressant and psychological-treatment options selected through shared decision making. They do not establish PsychSim's exact game-point magnitudes or medication-fit modifiers.

Developer opinion and provisional game balance assign 200 base care points to one reviewed first-line antidepressant. Medication-specific fit remains separately itemized and smaller; patient review may retune the exact values.

Developer opinion: for this initial outpatient snapshot, starting multiple antidepressants for one focal indication is a materially less parsimonious plan. The provisional game rule does not establish a universal combination-treatment or cross-titration rule.

Developer opinion: this short initial-outpatient snapshot is authored as major depressive disorder. Selecting a bipolar-spectrum diagnosis despite the case-authored negative mania history is treated as a potentially dangerous case-specific diagnostic error for this prototype; exact point magnitudes are game-balance values.

options.label: Major depressive disorder
options.explanation: This matches the case-authored primary diagnosis for the focused encounter snapshot.

omission.label: Primary diagnosis omitted
omission.explanation: The final answer did not identify the case-authored primary diagnosis.

misclassificationRules.label: Bipolar-spectrum misclassification
misclassificationRules.explanation: For this case-authored snapshot, a bipolar-spectrum label conflicts with the case-authored longitudinal history and can substantially redirect management.

additionalSelectionPolicy.label: Unsupported additional diagnoses
additionalSelectionPolicy.explanation: Additional diagnosis labels that do not match an authored alternative add a capped parsimony deduction.

workupObjectives.label: Establish episode duration and impairment
workupObjectives.explanationObtained: Essential and obtained: episode duration and functional impairment were established.
workupObjectives.explanationOmitted: Critical item omitted: episode duration and functional impairment were not established.

workupObjectives.label: Characterize the depressive symptom cluster
workupObjectives.explanationObtained: Essential and obtained: depressive symptoms and impairment were characterized.
workupObjectives.explanationOmitted: Critical item omitted: the depressive syndrome was not characterized.

workupObjectives.label: Screen for prior mania or hypomania
workupObjectives.explanationObtained: Essential and obtained: an appropriate negative bipolar-spectrum screen earns full credit.
workupObjectives.explanationOmitted: Critical item omitted: prior mania or hypomania was not assessed before antidepressant selection.

workupObjectives.label: Assess suicide risk and outpatient suitability
workupObjectives.explanationObtained: Essential and obtained: suicide risk and outpatient suitability were assessed.
workupObjectives.explanationOmitted: Critical item omitted: suicide risk and level of care were not assessed.

workupObjectives.label: Reconcile medications before prescribing
workupObjectives.explanationObtained: High-yield and obtained: the previously unreconciled medication list was verified.

workupObjectives.label: Review allergies and adverse reactions before prescribing
workupObjectives.explanationObtained: Allergy and adverse-reaction history was reviewed.
workupObjectives.explanationOmitted: Allergy and adverse-reaction history was not reviewed.

workupObjectives.label: Assess substance contribution
workupObjectives.explanationObtained: High-yield and obtained: substance use and withdrawal were assessed as possible contributors.
workupObjectives.explanationOmitted: Substance contribution was not assessed; no omission penalty applies in this prototype case.

treatmentWorkupRequirements.explanationMet: Prior mania or hypomania was assessed before antidepressant treatment.
treatmentWorkupRequirements.explanationMissing: Prior mania or hypomania was not assessed before antidepressant treatment.

treatmentWorkupRequirements.explanationMet: The medication list was reconciled before a medication was started.
treatmentWorkupRequirements.explanationMissing: The medication list was not reconciled before a medication was started.

treatmentWorkupRequirements.explanationMet: Allergies and adverse reactions were reviewed before a medication was started.
treatmentWorkupRequirements.explanationMissing: Allergies and adverse reactions were not reviewed before a medication was started.

treatmentGrades.label: Multiple antidepressants started together
treatmentGrades.explanation: For this initial outpatient snapshot, simultaneously starting two or more antidepressants is scored as a harmful, nonparsimonious shotgun regimen. This case rule does not generalize to cross-titration or established combination treatment.

treatmentGrades.label: Antipsychotic monotherapy for uncomplicated depression
treatmentGrades.explanation: Harmful: this uncomplicated first presentation does not support antipsychotic monotherapy, and the added adverse-effect burden is avoidable.

treatmentGrades.label: Buspirone monotherapy
treatmentGrades.explanation: Weak: buspirone monotherapy does not adequately address this depressive syndrome.

treatmentGrades.label: One reviewed first-line antidepressant
treatmentGrades.explanation: Broad first-line baseline: one reviewed antidepressant satisfies the dominant initial-medication decision for this focused outpatient snapshot. Medication-specific fit and safety remain separate traceable layers.

treatmentPathways.label: One first-line antidepressant plus outpatient care
treatmentPathways.explanation: Focused history supports a single starter antidepressant with psychotherapy and outpatient care.

treatmentPathways.label: Safe external evaluation
treatmentPathways.explanation: External evaluation is safe but offers less clinic value than routine treatment within scope.

scoreRules.label: Evidence-based psychotherapy
scoreRules.explanationIfTrue: Evidence-based psychotherapy was included in the combined plan.
scoreRules.explanationIfFalse: A psychotherapy option was omitted from the combined plan.

scoreRules.label: Behavioral activation
scoreRules.explanationIfTrue: A concrete behavioral activation plan supports recovery while treatment begins.
scoreRules.explanationIfFalse: No behavioral activation plan was selected.

scoreRules.label: Appropriate outpatient disposition
scoreRules.explanationIfTrue: Close outpatient follow-up matches the assessed level of care.
scoreRules.explanationIfFalse: The chosen disposition is safe when it is an available referral, but is less proportionate to this presentation.

scoreRules.label: Urgent medical escalation
scoreRules.explanationIfTrue: Urgent medical escalation is safe but disproportionate to the facts established in this encounter.
scoreRules.explanationIfFalse: Urgent medical escalation was not selected.

scoreRules.label: Emergency-department escalation
scoreRules.explanationIfTrue: Emergency transfer is a major mismatch for the stable facts established in this encounter and consumes a much higher level of care without an identified indication.

scoreRules.label: Avoid simultaneous multi-antidepressant starts
scoreRules.explanationIfTrue: For this initial outpatient snapshot, multiple antidepressants were started together for the same focal treatment decision.
scoreRules.explanationIfFalse: The final plan avoids a simultaneous multi-antidepressant start.
scoreRules.safetyErrorIfTrue: Multiple antidepressants were started together in this initial outpatient plan.

scoreRules.label: Avoid low-yield advanced testing
scoreRules.explanationIfTrue: Advanced testing added cost without a case-specific clue or treatment requirement.
scoreRules.explanationIfFalse: The workup avoided unsupported advanced testing.

referenceSolutions.label: Database plan
referenceSolutions.explanation: Uses focused history, one reviewed first-line antidepressant, psychotherapy, behavioral activation, and outpatient follow-up.

referenceSolutions.label: Equivalent first-line example
referenceSolutions.explanation: Uses the same focused workup and combined-care plan with an equivalent first-line antidepressant example.

referenceSolutions.label: Shotgun testing
referenceSolutions.explanation: Reaches the same treatment but buys every available history, examination, laboratory, and imaging option.

referenceSolutions.label: Unsafe treatment
referenceSolutions.explanation: Starts duplicate SSRI treatment and omits the nonmedication components of the plan.
